title: Notary part b: warrant.py audit fails without the operator's fingerprint (decision 4)
description: Proposed by track 2 on 2026-08-16 and ratified on 2026-10-21. Today audit without --expect exits 0 and only marks itself UNVERIFIED in its JSON.
acceptance_criteria: warrant.py audit without --expect still prints its report marked UNVERIFIED, and exits with a distinct, documented nonzero code. With a matching --expect it exits 0; with a mismatching one it fails as today.

Every caller in the repository that relied on exit 0 is found and adjusted: tests, scripts, skills and documentation examples. If a caller sits in a file another task holds a lock on, do not edit it; list it in the handoff.
A test pins each of the three cases.

The tool's help or the operator documentation states the operator's manual step: keep the root fingerprint outside the working tree by signing one git tag that carries it, with the exact command. The task never runs it and never signs anything.
Do not edit CLAUDE.md. The suite passes via goal_mode. Hand off to verifier.

notes.note: plan: add distinct documented nonzero exit code for audit --expect-less UNVERIFIED report (keep ALARM=3); pin with 3 tests; add git-tag command to warrant.py help + OPERATOR-ENROLMENT.md; grep found no code callers relying on exit 0, only a test_warrant.py assertion to update

EXPECTED: audit without --expect must mark UNVERIFIED and exit a distinct documented nonzero code (not 0, not 3/ALARM); matching --expect exits 0; mismatching --expect still exits 3 as before. ACTUAL: added EXIT_OK=0/EXIT_REFUSED=2/EXIT_ALARM=3/EXIT_DETECTOR_FAILED=4/EXIT_AUDIT_UNVERIFIED=5 to warrant.py, main() now returns EXIT_AUDIT_UNVERIFIED when out['UNVERIFIED'] is set (checked after ALARM so an orphan-ALARM on an unverified run still reports 3, unchanged). Documented in 'warrant.py audit --help' epilog and in .harness/OPERATOR-ENROLMENT.md. Replay: python3 .harness/bin/warrant.py audit --help  (shows exit-code table + git-tag command); python3 .harness/bin/warrant.py --root <scratch>/.harness audit  -> rc=5, JSON has UNVERIFIED, no ALARM (verified manually against a throwaway un-enrolled root). Caller search: grep -rn 'warrant.py audit|w.audit|w.main' across *.py/*.md/*.sh found zero code callers relying on exit 0 other than one test_warrant.py assertion (updated); no skills/ or .agents/skills/ files mention warrant.py at all; attest.py/roster.py only mention audit in prose (no subprocess call), left untouched (attest.py also locked by T-448). W-002-BRIEFING.md already states the ratified exit-code behavior correctly in its own prose quoting the ruling; left unedited since no fix was needed and it is not a file I hold a lock on. Operator's manual step (git tag, never run): added warrant.TAG_COMMAND = git tag -s harness-trust-root -m "SHA256:<fingerprint from `warrant.py anchor`>", printed in 'audit --help' epilog and in OPERATOR-ENROLMENT.md; an AST-based test (T450OperatorTagStep.test_no_call_in_the_module_invokes_git) asserts no argv in warrant.py starts with git. Tests added: T450AuditExitCodes (no-expect->5, matching-expect->0, mismatching-expect->3, three codes pairwise distinct) and T450OperatorTagStep (command appears in --help and in an operator doc, never executed); updated the pre-existing test that pinned exit 0 for the unenrolled/no-expect case (ThirdPanelRegressions.test_unenrolled_without_expect_stays_exit_zero_and_says_not_assessed -> renamed test_unenrolled_without_expect_is_unverified_not_silent, now asserts EXIT_AUDIT_UNVERIFIED). Did not touch CLAUDE.md. Suite: python3 .harness/bin/goal_mode.py run --cmd 'python3 -m pytest .harness/tests -q' -> GOAL REACHED on iteration 1/3 (104.76s), full suite green. Doc note for CLAUDE.md maintainers (not applied by me per protocol): claude.md's Identity Gate bullet still reads 'audit --expect SHA256:...' without mentioning the new distinct exit code for the no-expect path; worth a line at the next harness-update pass.

HANDOFF -> verifier: Replay: (1) python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_warrant.py -q -> 76 passed (was 73 before, +3 net: one case renamed/strengthened, two new classes T450AuditExitCodes [4 tests] and T450OperatorTagStep [4 tests]). (2) python3 .harness/bin/goal_mode.py run --cmd "python3 -m pytest .harness/tests -q" -> GOAL REACHED iteration 1/3, full suite green. (3) python3 .harness/bin/warrant.py audit --help -> prints exit-code table (0/3/4/5) and the operator's git-tag command verbatim. (4) mkdir -p <scratch>/.harness && python3 .harness/bin/warrant.py --root <scratch>/.harness audit ; echo rc=$? -> rc=5, JSON carries UNVERIFIED, no ALARM (manually verified, not just via pytest). (5) grep -rn 'warrant.py audit\|w\.audit\|w\.main' . --include=*.py --include=*.md --include=*.sh (excluding .git) to confirm no other caller relies on exit 0; only test_warrant.py did, and it is updated. Acceptance criteria from T-450.json addressed point by point: (a) audit w/o --expect -> UNVERIFIED + distinct documented nonzero exit (EXIT_AUDIT_UNVERIFIED=5); matching --expect -> 0; mismatching --expect -> 3 (ALARM, unchanged); (b) caller search done, only test_warrant.py needed adjusting, no scripts/skills/docs relied on exit 0 (OPERATOR-ENROLMENT.md had no claim about that row at all -- added one for accuracy, not because it was wrong); (c) three cases pinned in T450AuditExitCodes plus a pairwise-distinctness test; (d) operator's manual step (one signed git tag carrying the fingerprint, kept outside the working tree) stated with the exact command in warrant.py's audit --help epilog AND in OPERATOR-ENROLMENT.md -- never run, never signed (AST test T450OperatorTagStep.test_no_call_in_the_module_invokes_git enforces warrant.py never shells out to git); (e) CLAUDE.md untouched, suite passes via goal_mode. Note for the record: attest.py's docstring/help text that mentions 'audit --expect' was left untouched because it is locked by T-448, listed per instructions, not edited. W-002-BRIEFING.md already states the new exit-code behavior correctly from the ruling it quotes, so no edit was needed there either. One documentation gap flagged but NOT fixed (CLAUDE.md is governed, not mine to edit): the Identity Gate bullet describes audit --expect but not the new distinct exit code for the no-expect path -- worth a line at the next harness evolution pass.

VERIFIED by replay (verifier-g10-audit, different agent from producer worker-g10-audit). (1) python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_warrant.py -q -> 76 passed (matches producer claim). (2) python3 .harness/bin/goal_mode.py run --cmd "python3 -m pytest .harness/tests -q" -> GOAL REACHED iteration 1/3 (112.71s), full suite green. (3) Manual exit-code replay on a throwaway un-enrolled root (mkdir -p <scratch>/.harness; warrant.py --root <scratch>/.harness audit) -> rc=5, JSON carries UNVERIFIED, no ALARM. (4) Ran T450AuditExitCodes + T450OperatorTagStep directly (pytest -k T450) -> 8 passed, confirming no-expect->5, matching-expect->0, mismatching-expect->3 (EXIT_ALARM), pairwise distinctness, tag command present verbatim in  output (confirmed by running --help myself) and in OPERATOR-ENROLMENT.md (confirmed via git diff), and an AST walk proves warrant.py never argv[0]=='git'. (5) Caller search via grep -rln 'warrant.py audit' across the repo (excluding .git): only prose mentions in attest.py/roster.py/docs/ruling files, no subprocess caller relies on exit 0 anywhere; confirmed attest.py and roster.py mention audit only in docstrings/comments, no subprocess.run call. Also grepped skills/.agents/.claude SKILL.md files for 'warrant.py audit': none found. (6) CLAUDE.md untouched: git diff --stat HEAD -- CLAUDE.md -> empty. (7) MUTATION TEST (cognitive-diversity angle, different from producer's method): copied .harness into a throwaway tempdir outside the working tree, edited the copy's warrant.py so audit returns EXIT_OK instead of EXIT_AUDIT_UNVERIFIED when out['UNVERIFIED'] is set, reran pytest on the copy -> T450AuditExitCodes::test_no_expect_is_unverified_and_exits_distinctly_nonzero and ThirdPanelRegressions::test_unenrolled_without_expect_is_unverified_not_silent both FAILED with AssertionError: 0 != 5, proving the suite catches the regression the task guards against. (One unrelated failure, NoPrivateKeyIsEverTracked, is copy-environment noise -- that test shells out to git ls-files and the throwaway copy is not a git repo; it is not a mutation-survival signal and reproduces on the unmutated copy too.) WEAKNESS noted but not blocking: the audit() docstring at warrant.py ~line 808-810 still says 'Exit stays 0 here on purpose' for the un-enrolled+no-expect case; that sentence predates T-450 and is now stale since main() returns EXIT_AUDIT_UNVERIFIED(5) for that case today -- worth a one-line comment fix in a follow-up, does not affect any acceptance criterion or test. All five T-450 acceptance criteria satisfied by independent replay.
